description.en: Ontology module for textile durability constructs, durability-related performance characteristics, degradation phenomena, external damage and failure modes. Test methods, observations, measurement results, thresholds and values remain in the textile assessment module.

comments.en: The module keeps Durability and IntrinsicDurability as explicit OWL classes and represents observed performance parameters and failure modes as OWL classes rather than SKOS concepts.

sourceLocator.value: CIRPASS Textile Ontology modelling specification, version 1.1.0.

bibliographicCitation.value: EU DPP Textile Durability Ontology. Version 1.1.2.

modellingNote.value: Wrinkling affects the interpretation of intrinsic durability depending on product type, use context and acceptable thresholds.

sourceLocator.value: JRC Annex 13.10.1, printed page 468, lines 11065-11071; Annex 13.4, Table 124, printed pages 362-367 where applicable.

comment.en: Durability-related deformation behaviour describing the tendency of a textile material or product to form creases under use or after deformation and recovery cycles.

sourceLocator.value: JRC Preparatory Study, Section 6.4.1, printed page 87, lines 2277-2279; JRC Preparatory Study, Section 13.10.1.1, printed page 469, lines 11092-11094.

comment.en: Component failure mode involving failure of trims or auxiliary components associated with a textile product.

sourceLocator.value: CIRPASS Textile Ontology modelling specification, version 1.1.0.

comment.en: Category of observed performance parameters related to surface behaviour or surface degradation.

modellingNote.value: Fabric smoothness is represented as an observed performance parameter. A measured value or inspection grade should be represented in the assessment module, while rough or stiff fabric is modelled as a failure expression.

sourceLocator.value: CIRPASS Textile Ontology modelling specification, version 1.1.0.

comment.en: Observed performance parameter describing the visible or tactile smoothness of a fabric surface, commonly considered during visual inspection after washing, drying or other durability-related stress.

sourceLocator.value: JRC Preparatory Study, Section 6.4.1, printed page 87, lines 2277-2279; JRC Preparatory Study, Section 13.10.1.1, printed page 469, lines 11092-11093.

comment.en: Specific seam failure involving a hole or localised opening at or around a seam.

modellingNote.value: Fabric strength is modelled as reducing the likelihood of tear or rip under comparable conditions, rather than as negatively affecting tear or rip.
Fabric strength contributes to the interpretation of intrinsic durability as an aggregated mechanical performance parameter.

sourceLocator.value: JRC Annex 13.10.1, printed page 468, lines 11065-11071; Annex 13.4, Table 124, printed pages 362-367 where applicable.

comment.en: Aggregated observed mechanical performance parameter describing the strength of a fabric, potentially covering tensile strength, tear strength or bursting strength depending on the test context.

sourceLocator.value: CIRPASS Textile Ontology modelling specification, version 1.1.0.

comment.en: Category of observed performance parameters related to seams, assembly or garment construction.

sourceLocator.value: JRC Annex 13.10.1, printed page 468, lines 11065-11071; Annex 13.4, Table 124, printed pages 362-367 where applicable.

comment.en: Durability construct based on the physical and measurable ability of a textile product to maintain relevant performance characteristics over time under specified use, maintenance or test conditions.

modellingNote.value: Loss of comfort is kept as a functional failure mode. Specific causes may include roughness, stiffness, loss of elasticity, poor breathability, poor insulation or other context-dependent phenomena.

sourceLocator.value: CIRPASS Textile Ontology modelling specification, version 1.1.0.

comment.en: Functional failure mode corresponding to loss of comfort or comfort-related suitability during use, maintenance or ageing.

sourceLocator.value: JRC Preparatory Study, Section 6.4.1, printed page 87, lines 2273-2274.

comment.en: Specific trim failure involving failure of a zipper or zip fastener.

sourceLocator.value: CIRPASS Textile Ontology modelling specification, version 1.1.0.

comment.en: Category of failure modes primarily involving rupture, tearing or mechanical damage.

modellingNote.value: Elasticity loss is kept distinct from loss of dimensional stability. A product may lose elastic recovery without necessarily being described primarily as dimensionally unstable.

sourceLocator.value: CIRPASS Textile Ontology modelling specification, version 1.1.0.

comment.en: Structural failure mode corresponding to loss of elasticity, elastic recovery or stretch-related functionality of a textile product or fabric.

sourceLocator.value: CIRPASS Textile Ontology modelling specification, version 1.1.0.

comment.en: Durability-related product characteristic that can be observed, assessed or measured to evaluate physical durability. It denotes the characteristic type, not a test, observation, result or quantitative value.

modellingNote.value: This class is available for strict failure modes. Pilling and fuzzing/matting are intentionally kept as observed degradation phenomena when they are used as inspection parameters.

sourceLocator.value: CIRPASS Textile Ontology modelling specification, version 1.1.0.

comment.en: Category of failure modes primarily affecting the textile surface. Borderline surface phenomena that are also assessed as performance parameters should remain under ObservedDegradationPhenomenon to preserve the module disjointness pattern.

sourceLocator.value: JRC Preparatory Study, Section 13.10.1.1, printed page 469, lines 11089-11093; JRC Preparatory Study, Section 6.4.1, printed page 87, lines 2277-2279.

comment.en: Aggregated failure mode. It may be decomposed later into more specific phenomena such as fraying, thinning, localised wear or hole formation.

sourceLocator.value: JRC Preparatory Study, Section 6.4.1, printed page 87, lines 2277-2279; JRC Preparatory Study, Section 13.10.1.1, printed page 469, lines 11091-11092.

comment.en: Failure expression corresponding to loss of the ability of a textile product or fabric to retain its dimensions after use, laundering or treatment cycles.

sourceLocator.value: JRC Preparatory Study, Section 6.4.1, printed page 87, lines 2277-2279; JRC Preparatory Study, Section 13.10.1.1, printed page 469, lines 11091-11092.

comment.en: Logo failure may also be interpreted as a component-related failure depending on whether the logo is printed, embroidered or applied as a separate component. It is kept under visual failure mode in this module.

modellingNote.value: Introduced to keep surface degradation phenomena separate from strict FailureMode, because the ontology declares FailureMode and ObservedPerformanceParameter disjoint at high level.

sourceLocator.value: CIRPASS Textile Ontology modelling specification, version 1.1.0.

comment.en: Observed degradation phenomenon affecting the surface condition of a textile material or product, such as pilling, fuzzing or matting.

sourceLocator.value: CIRPASS Textile Ontology modelling specification, version 1.1.0.

comment.en: Observable phenomenon indicating physical deterioration of a textile material or product. It is distinct from the performance characteristic used to assess resistance to that deterioration.

modellingNote.value: Through the alignment txtdur:Durability rdfs:subClassOf dpp:Durability, this class inherits dpp:QualityIndicator and dpp:QuantitativeProperty. This is an inherited EU DPP Core commitment: it does not make a durability instance a numeric value. Numerical observations and results remain represented through Textile Assessment and txtcon:QuantitativeValue.

sourceLocator.value: JRC Annex 13.10.1, printed page 468, lines 11065-11067.

comment.en: Ability of a product to maintain over time its function and performance under specified conditions of use, maintenance and repair.

modellingNote.value: Seam slippage negatively affects the interpretation of intrinsic durability as a loss of assembly performance.

sourceLocator.value: JRC Annex 13.10.1, printed page 468, lines 11065-11071; Annex 13.4, Table 124, printed pages 362-367 where applicable.

comment.en: Durability-related assembly performance characteristic describing displacement of yarns at or near a seam under mechanical stress, which may lead to deformation or opening.

sourceLocator.value: CIRPASS Textile Ontology modelling specification, version 1.1.0.

comment.en: Category of failure modes affecting components or trims.

sourceLocator.value: JRC Section 9.2.1.3, printed pages 112-113, lines 2968-3010.

comment.en: Progressive change or degradation of textile product performance over time under repeated use, care, environmental exposure or stress.

sourceLocator.value: JRC Section 12.3.16, printed page 254, lines 7150-7157.

comment.en: Degradation of textile material or product properties associated with ultraviolet or other relevant radiation exposure.

modellingNote.value: The concept is modelled as a tactile failure mode rather than as a structural characteristic. The corresponding structural or tactile fabric property remains outside this module.

sourceLocator.value: CIRPASS Textile Ontology modelling specification, version 1.1.0.

comment.en: Failure mode in which a fabric becomes or is perceived as rough, stiff or unpleasant to touch, affecting user acceptance and comfort-related use.

modellingNote.value: Introduced to avoid forcing tactile failures such as rough or stiff fabric into purely visual or purely structural categories.

sourceLocator.value: CIRPASS Textile Ontology modelling specification, version 1.1.0.

comment.en: Category of failure modes primarily affecting tactile perception, hand feel or comfort-related touch properties of a textile product or fabric.

modellingNote.value: Observed abrasion resistance contributes to the interpretation of intrinsic durability but is not equivalent to intrinsic durability.

sourceLocator.value: JRC Annex 13.10.1, printed page 468, lines 11065-11071; Annex 13.4, Table 124, printed pages 362-367 where applicable.

comment.en: Observed performance parameter describing the resistance of a textile material or product to wear caused by rubbing or abrasion.

sourceLocator.value: CIRPASS Textile Ontology modelling specification, version 1.1.0.

comment.en: Category of observed performance parameters related to mechanical resistance or strength.

sourceLocator.value: CIRPASS Textile Ontology modelling specification, version 1.1.0.

comment.en: Category of observed performance parameters related to visual appearance or colour behaviour.

sourceLocator.value: JRC Annex 13.10.1, printed page 469, lines 11089-11094.

comment.en: Structural or assembly-related failure mode involving loss of seam integrity or seam functionality.

sourceLocator.value: JRC Preparatory Study, Annex 13.10.1.1, printed page 469, lines 11090-11091.

comment.en: Mechanical failure mode involving rupture, tearing or ripping of textile material under stress, snagging or damage.

sourceLocator.value: CIRPASS Textile Ontology modelling specification, version 1.1.0.

comment.en: Category of observed performance parameters related to deformation, shape retention or dimensional behaviour.

sourceLocator.value: CIRPASS Textile Ontology modelling specification, version 1.1.0.

comment.en: Damage caused by external or accidental events during product use, not necessarily resulting from intrinsic lack of durability.

modellingNote.value: Observed colour fastness contributes to the interpretation of intrinsic durability, while colour fading is a failure expression.
Colour fastness is the resistance parameter; colour fading is a typical visual failure expression of its degradation.

sourceLocator.value: JRC Annex 13.10.1, printed page 468, lines 11065-11071; Annex 13.4, Table 124, printed pages 362-367 where applicable.

comment.en: Observed performance parameter describing the resistance of a textile colour to fading, running or alteration under conditions such as washing, rubbing, perspiration or light exposure.

modellingNote.value: Dimensional stability contributes to the interpretation of intrinsic durability; loss of dimensional stability is the corresponding failure expression.
Dimensional stability is the performance parameter; loss of dimensional stability is the corresponding failure expression.

sourceLocator.value: JRC Section 11.1.1.1, printed page 186, lines 5267-5273; Annex 13.10.1, printed page 469, lines 11089-11094.

comment.en: Observed performance parameter describing the ability of a textile product or fabric to retain its dimensions after use, laundering or other treatment cycles.

sourceLocator.value: CIRPASS Textile Ontology modelling specification, version 1.1.0.

comment.en: Category of failure modes primarily affecting structure, integrity or dimensional behaviour.

modellingNote.value: The research gap used the wording 'fuzzing/melting', but the JRC and referenced ISO standards use fuzzing/matting. This ontology therefore introduces FuzzingOrMatting and avoids the unsupported term melting.
FuzzingOrMatting is not made a subclass of FailureMode because it is modelled following the existing pilling pattern as an observed degradation phenomenon used in performance inspection.

sourceLocator.value: CIRPASS Textile Ontology modelling specification, version 1.1.0.

comment.en: Observed surface degradation phenomenon involving fuzzing or matting of the fabric surface. The term follows the JRC and ISO wording 'fuzzing or matting', not 'melting'.

sourceLocator.value: CIRPASS Textile Ontology modelling specification, version 1.1.0.

comment.en: Category of failure modes primarily affecting visible appearance.

modellingNote.value: Colour depth and evenness is distinct from colour fastness. Colour fastness concerns resistance to fading, running or alteration, whereas colour depth/evenness concerns the achieved visual colour quality.

sourceLocator.value: CIRPASS Textile Ontology modelling specification, version 1.1.0.

comment.en: Observed visual performance parameter describing the depth and evenness of colour in a textile product or fabric, especially in relation to dyeing and finishing quality.

modellingNote.value: Introduced to represent failure modes that are not adequately captured by visual, structural, mechanical or component failure categories alone.

sourceLocator.value: CIRPASS Textile Ontology modelling specification, version 1.1.0.

comment.en: Category of failure modes primarily involving loss of intended use, comfort or functional suitability of a textile product.

modellingNote.value: Accidental damage may result in tear or rip, but this is not a necessary relation in every case.

sourceLocator.value: JRC Preparatory Study, Section 6.4.1, printed page 87, lines 2277-2279; JRC Preparatory Study, Section 13.10.1.1, printed page 469, lines 11090-11091.

comment.en: External damage occurring during use, such as accidental tearing, ripping or staining, which may lead to product rejection or disposal.

sourceLocator.value: JRC Preparatory Study, Section 13.10.1.1, printed page 469, lines 11089-11093; JRC Preparatory Study, Section 6.4.1, printed page 87, lines 2276-2279.

comment.en: Visual failure mode corresponding to progressive loss of colour intensity during use, washing, ageing or exposure.

modellingNote.value: Observed pilling negatively affects the interpretation of intrinsic durability; pilling resistance, if modelled separately, should be represented as a protective characteristic.
Observed pilling may contribute to fabric breakdown as part of a progressive surface degradation process, but it should not be treated as the sole necessary cause of fabric breakdown.

sourceLocator.value: JRC Annex 13.10.1, printed page 468, lines 11065-11071; Annex 13.4, Table 124, printed pages 362-367 where applicable.

comment.en: Observed surface degradation phenomenon involving the formation of small balls or pills of entangled fibres on a textile surface during wear, friction, use or testing.

sourceLocator.value: JRC Preparatory Study, Section 6.4.1, printed page 87, lines 2277-2279; JRC Preparatory Study, Section 13.10.1.1, printed page 469, lines 11092-11093.

comment.en: Kept distinct from colour fading because discolouration may be localised, irregular or caused by specific use or exposure conditions.

modellingNote.value: Pilling resistance is separated from Pilling.

sourceLocator.value: JRC Annex 13.10.1, printed page 468, lines 11065-11071; Annex 13.4, Table 124, printed pages 362-367 where applicable.

comment.en: Durability-related performance characteristic describing the ability of a textile material, fabric or product to resist the formation of pills under friction, wear or use conditions.

sourceLocator.value: CIRPASS Textile Ontology modelling specification, version 1.1.0.

comment.en: Failure modes are kept separate from observed performance parameters. For example, colour fastness is a parameter, while colour fading is a failure mode.

sourceLocator.value: CIRPASS Textile Ontology modelling specification, version 1.1.0.

comment.en: Relates a textile product to a failure mode observed, expected or considered relevant for that product.

sourceLocator.value: CIRPASS Textile Ontology modelling specification, version 1.1.0.

comment.en: Relates a textile product to an observed performance parameter relevant to its durability assessment.

sourceLocator.value: CIRPASS Textile Ontology modelling specification, version 1.1.0.

comment.en: Relates a product to a degradation phenomenon observed or considered relevant for that product. A concrete observation, test and result should be represented in the textile assessment module.

sourceLocator.value: CIRPASS Textile Ontology modelling specification, version 1.1.0.

comment.en: Indicates that external damage may result in a failure mode.

sourceLocator.value: CIRPASS Textile Ontology modelling specification, version 1.1.0.

comment.en: Relates an observed performance parameter to a failure mode that expresses degradation or loss of that parameter.

sourceLocator.value: CIRPASS Textile Ontology modelling specification, version 1.1.0.

comment.en: Relates a textile product to a durability aspect relevant to its assessment or declaration.

sourceLocator.value: CIRPASS Textile Ontology modelling specification, version 1.1.0.

comment.en: Relates a textile product or product observation to external damage occurring during use.

sourceLocator.value: CIRPASS Textile Ontology modelling specification, version 1.1.0.

comment.en: Indicates that a failure mode, degradation phenomenon or damage negatively affects a durability-related aspect.

sourceLocator.value: CIRPASS Textile Ontology modelling specification, version 1.1.0.

comment.en: Relates a durability-related performance characteristic to a degradation phenomenon that expresses deterioration of that characteristic. This is an instance-level relation and is not a deterministic causal axiom.
